messages.subject: shinydashboard sidebar menu dynamically created not work with conditionalPanel
messages.subject_clean: shinydashboard sidebar menu dynamically created not work with conditionalPanel
messages.body_plain:
conditionalPanel works fairly reliably in the shinydashboard sidebar as excellently documented here <https://rstudio.github.io/shinydashboard/structure.html>.  However, to my chagrin, it fails me or more likely nowadays I fail it.  Here is the code to illustrate my point.

The sidebarMenu is given an id="sbm", I wish to display a hr() if the "Tab 2" is clicked.  The conditionalPanel can be put in either ui or server function, the hr won't display.  In my browser inspect id="sbm" is nowhere to be found.  Instead, the "menu" appears to be the id (see the attachment).  The hr() still refuses to appear even I use the menu as id.

I tried to do the same thing not using dynamically generated sidebar menu, I can see id="sbm" exactly where I expected to see.

So my questions are

why the sidebarMenu id couldn't be assigned, instead the name of ouput$xxx object is used as id
how to create conditionalPanel in sidebar menu when sidebar menu is dynamically generated

Any insight and advice is greatly appreciated.

==================================
library(shiny)
library(shinydashboard)

ui <- dashboardPage(
  dashboardHeader(title = "Dynamic sidebar"),
  dashboardSidebar(
    sidebarMenuOutput("menu")
    ,conditionalPanel(condition = "input.sbm == 'tab2'", hr())
  ),
  dashboardBody()
)

server <- function(input, output) {
  output$menu <- renderMenu({
    sidebarMenu(id = "sbm",
      menuItem("Home", tabName="tabHome", icon = icon("home")),
      menuItem("Tab 2", tabName="tab2", icon = icon("calendar"))
      # ,conditionalPanel(condition = "input.sbm == 'tab2'", hr())
      # ,conditionalPanel(condition = "input$sbm == 'tab2'", hr())
    )
  })
}

messages.subject: Attaching validate(need()) error messages directly to inputs
messages.subject_clean: Attaching validate(need()) error messages directly to inputs
messages.body_plain:
Hey everyone,

I've written quite a large app and I'm now going through the process of cleaning things up and adding proper error messages using validate(need()). The really nice thing about writing error messages this way is that they propagate throughout the app, with any downstream objects or plots also displaying the same error.

I'm having a bit of an issue though, because I have some inputs which need to take particular values, or the app will produce errors (i.e. numeric inputs which can only take positive values). What's more, I call these inputs a hundred or so times throughout the app, and often dynamically - i.e. input[[paste0("number", i)]]. So if I have to write error messages every time a reactive object or output uses the input, I would end up writing similar chunks of code hundreds of times throughout the app - something like validate(need(input$number1 >= 1, "Error: the input must be positive". And things are even more complicated when I write the error messages for when the input is called dynamically. And of course this completey misses what's so nice about the validate(need()) system.

So what I'm wondering if is there's any way to attach or associate a validate() style warning message directly with an input? This way, I would only have to write the error message once, and it would propagate throughout the app every time the input is called.

The closest I can think of getting to this would be to set up all the inputs like this:
ui.R:
numericInput("number1", "Enter number 1:")

server.R:
number1 <- reactive({
x <- input$number1
validate(need(x >= 1, "Error: the input must be positive))
return(x)
})

And then in the rest of the server, you can just call number1() instead of input$number1 to get the error message.

But I just thought I'd check if there is a better way of doing this. Especially since, as I mentioned, I often call these inputs dynamically, so implementing this throughout the app is not simply a case of "find all and replace".

Cheers,
John

messages.subject: Local Shiny app -- subdirectory issue
messages.subject_clean: Local Shiny app -- subdirectory issue
messages.body_plain:
I have a sample Shiny server running on my local machine, but I want to use the directory to host multiple apps. One app at a time seems just fine, but errors with the directory structure is as follows:

/ShinyApp /www index.html /hello ui.R server.R

When I go to http://mycomputername:port, the index.html file shows. Going to http://mycomputername:port/hello returns:

ERROR: cannot open the connection

messages.subject: Re: Modularizing Shiny app and map_shape_click not working
messages.subject_clean: Modularizing Shiny app and map_shape_click not working
messages.body_plain:
I just finished creating a module for  the leaflet section of a dashboard I'm building last night.   I chose to build the module with both the UI and the server component in it.   One of things I had to do was to ensure that anytime in the UI that I was going to implement a an output, that I encapsulated the id with ns().   Example:

tagList(
 fluidRow(leafletOutput(ns(
 "locationSiteMap"
 ),
 height = 1024)
 , width = 12) ,
 absolutePanel(
 top = 100,
 right = 20,
 selectInput(
 ns("locationType"),
 "Location Type",
 choices = c(
 "CLINIC",
 "DEFAULT",
 "EXTERNAL",
 "HOSPITAL",
 "LAUNDRY",
 "OFFICE",
 "REMOTE"
 )
 ,
 multiple = TRUE,
 selectize = TRUE
 ) ,...

On the Server side, I also needed to make sure the right name space was used, by using session$ns(myId).  Example:
observeEvent(input$locationSiteMap_marker_click , {

    leafletProxy(session$ns("locationSiteMap")) %>% clearPopups()

    isolate({
      showSitePopup(
        input$locationSiteMap_marker_click$id,
        input$locationSiteMap_marker_click$lat,
        input$locationSiteMap_marker_click$lng
      )
    })
  })

So ensuring that the right prefix is attached to your id is important, and requires that both the UI and the server components have this handled.  Note that this was my second module, so I'm sure you will hear more details from our experts here.
Brett

messages.subject_clean: updateCheckboxGroupInput and updateCheckboxInput update differently
messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

Is there any explanations  why "updateCheckboxGroupInput" and "updateCheckboxInput" are
different in selection update?

"updateCheckboxInput" updates "label" and "value", while
"updateCheckboxGroupInput" updates only "choices" but not "selected" in the same simple code ( code is below and attached ).

Have somebody an idea?
Thank you in advance,
Kirill Essine

#**************************updateCheckboxInput*************************

library(shiny)
ui <-  mainPanel(

    checkboxInput( inputId = "Update",
                            label   = "Update selection",
                           value   = FALSE),

    checkboxInput( inputId  = "Select",
                              label  = "A",
                             value  = FALSE)
)

server <- function(input, output,session) {

  observeEvent (input$Update, {

     if(input$Update) {

       updateCheckboxInput(
                    session  = session,
                      inputId  = "Select",
                         label  = "B",
                        value  = TRUE)
     }
  })

}
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

#**************************updateCheckboxGroupInput*************************
library(shiny)
ui <-  mainPanel(

    checkboxInput( inputId = "Update",
                    label   = "Update selection",
                   value   = FALSE),

    checkboxGroupInput( inputId  = "Select",
                     label  = "Select",
                 choices  = c("A"=1,"B"=2),
                 selected = c(1,2),
                      inline = TRUE)
)

server <- function(input, output,session) {

  observeEvent (input$Update, {

     if(input$Update) {

       updateCheckboxGroupInput(
             session  = session,
              inputId  = "Select",
                 label  = NULL,
            choices  = c("C"=3,"D"=4),
            selected = c(3,4),
                 inline = TRUE)
     }
  })

}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.subject: Re: New shiny user questions
messages.subject_clean: New shiny user questions
messages.body_plain:
For #2, you have several options.

A. Make a ui.R (or ui value in app.R) as normal but include some custom HTML: either use includeHTML, or tag objects directly (see http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/html-tags.html).
B. Use the new HTML Templates feature to build large swaths of your app using custom HTML, but still use R to create input/output objects and for other things R might be better at. http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/templates.html
C. Use raw HTML for your UI. Mentioned for completeness, as I don't recommend this anymore as it only has drawbacks when compared to HTML Templates. http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/html-ui.html

https://github.com/rstudio/rmarkdown/pull/688 I cannot fix your
problem because I heard it was basically a user error, i.e. you set
the environment variable RSTUDIO_PANDOC to a wrong directory in your
app. You should not need to manipulate this environment since Shiny
Server will automatically set it to the correct location. If you
modify it, you should know what it means.

If your app does not work without setting RSTUDIO_PANDOC, that is
likely to be our problem, and we can definitely investigate it.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe,

This counts as exciting in my book :) Actually, a few guys at us might want to have a look at it. Is it already, say, at beta maturity? If yes, then I would appreciate some advise from you that what should we look at in the GitHub repo and what not yet. (Here I'm assuming that the code under development you talk about is available somewhere under https://github.com/rstudio/shiny, what may not be the case.)

Thanks, best regards
Imre

> We're actively working on this now; we've gotten past the tricky technical problems that have held us up in the past, so it's full steam ahead now. We hope to ship some useful functionality with the upcoming release of Shiny (in time for useR 2016) and some more stuff will come in the release after that.
>

> > > We made a couple of attempts, but were not happy with the results. Something we might revisit again in 2016. In the meantime a number of manual, non-native solutions have been attempted, including one I wrote:
> > > https://github.com/jcheng5/shiny-resume
> > >
> > > On Tue, Oct 6, 2015 at 1:51 PM Barry Grant <bar...@gmail.com> wrote:

> > > > Any updates on this "native support" capability?
> > > > Thanks!

> > > >
> > > >
> > > > On Tuesday, March 5, 2013 at 10:57:19 AM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:

> > > > >
> > > > > On Tuesday, March 5, 2013, wrote:

> > > > > > Hi all,
> > > > > >
> > > > > > we've been using shiny internally for (to use big words) "exploratory data analysis" in a project for some time and it's absolutely fabulous. However, working with a shiny application shows that there is a number of capabilities that "would be very nice to have". I understand that proper authentication (and maybe user management/authorization) will be introduced later - at least in the "enterprise edition". What I would be after now is saving and reloading session state.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > Two use cases as example:
> > > > > > - The user works on the data (effectively clicks around for some time, changing inputs) and finds just the visualization he wants. He closes the browser; next time when he opens it, he would like to see this state.
> > > > > > - The user wants to be able to record visualization states (for various "findings") and recall them one-by-one for a live, step-by-step demonstration.
> > > > > >
> > > > > > At some level, both cases boil down to the ability to save and load (full or partial) session states. I think that to some extent this can be done manually in the code (I haven't really had the time to think through and implement the tricks that seem to be applicable); my question is whether there is "platform support" or is it in the scope of future development at all.

On Thursday, 5 May 2016 07:11:49 UTC-7, bar...@rstudio.com wrote:
> Hi shiny folks,
>
> I’m a recent addition to the Shiny team at RStudio and I wanted to let you all know that we’ve just added a pretty exciting new feature to Shiny’s development version (install it with: devtools::install_github("rstudio/shiny”)).
>
> There’s two new functions: insertUI and removeUI, which allow you to add and remove arbitrary pieces of UI to your app. The best way to familiarize yourself with these might be to check out this demo app <https://beta.rstudioconnect.com/barbara/insertUI/> and read this article <http://shiny.rstudio-staging.com/articles/dynamic-ui.html>.
>
> We’re guessing that a lot of you might find this feature useful, so we’d really appreciate if you could try it out and lets us know if you encounter any problems (or just general feedback). We’re hoping to release to CRAN in the coming weeks.
>
>
> I’ll leave you with parts of the documentation and minimal examples:
>
> insertUI
>
> This function allows you to dynamically add an arbitrarily large UI object into your app, whenever you want, as many times as you want. Unlike renderUI, the UI generated with insertUI is not updatable as a whole: once it's created, it stays there. Each new call to insertUI creates more UI objects, in addition to the ones already there (all independent from one another). To update a part of the UI (ex: an input object), you must use the appropriate render function or a customized reactive function. To remove any part of your UI, use removeUI.
>
> Note that whatever UI object you pass through ui, it is always wrapped in an extra div (or if inline = TRUE, a span) before making its way into the DOM. This does not affect what you mean to do, and it makes it easier to remove the whole UI object using removeUI (if you wish to do so, of course).
>
> Example:
>
> ## Only run this example in interactive R sessions
> if (interactive()) {
> # Define UI
> ui <- fluidPage(
>   actionButton("add", "Add UI")
> )
>
> # Server logic
> server <- function(input, output, session) {
>   observeEvent(input$add, {
>     insertUI(
>       selector = "#add",
>       where = "afterEnd",
>       ui = textInput(paste0("txt", input$add),
>                      "Insert some text")
>     )
>   })
> }
>
> # Complete app with UI and server components
> shinyApp(ui, server)
> }
>
>
> removeUI
>
> This function allows you to remove any part of your UI. Once removeUI is executed on some element, it is gone forever. While it may be a particularly useful pattern to pair this with insertUI (to remove some UI you had previously inserted), there is no restriction on what you can use removeUI on. Any element that can be selected through a jQuery selector can be removed through this function.
>
> Example:
>
> ## Only run this example in interactive R sessions
> if (interactive()) {
> # Define UI
> ui <- fluidPage(
>   actionButton("rmv", "Remove UI"),
>   textInput("txt", "This is no longer useful")
> )
>
> # Server logic
> server <- function(input, output, session) {
>   observeEvent(input$rmv, {
>     removeUI(
>       selector = "div:has(> #txt)"
>     )
>   })
> }
>
> # Complete app with UI and server components
> shinyApp(ui, server)
> }
>

messages.subject_clean: Announcement: insertUI and removeUI functions now available on Shiny's development version
messages.body_plain:
Hi Dean,

Thanks for your feedback!

I think your first comment is a really good catch, I'll be sure to update the documentation to reflect that :)

As for the second suggestion, I definitely struggled with that. This <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/insertAdjacentHTML> is what the `where` argument was based off of. I totally understand your intuition and initially felt the same way. However, since `where` is always relative to the `selector`, I don't think there's a very elegant way to add elements after one another, instead of the more stack-like format that `afterEnd` produces. There is a workaround, however, which is to use `beforeEnd` instead -- `beforeEnd` makes newly inserted elements children of the `selector` element, so it's definitely a bad idea to use it is your `selector` is a button or something like that. But if your `selector` is a just a placeholder div, then, this produces the result you intended: `beforeEnd` always adds the new element as the *last* child of the `selector` element, so the visual result is that things get inserted one after another. This is actually why `beforeEnd` is the default. It is also the pattern I use for the demo app <https://beta.rstudioconnect.com/barbara/insertUI/> (use a placeholder as `selector` and stick to the `beforeEnd` default). Maybe I should make this clearer in the documentation or the article. Do you feel like this is enough flexibility for the user?

Thanks again, really helpful to get a pair of fresh eyes on this!
Barbara

Yes that's enough flexibility, and as I said I recognize it's something that might no really have an ideal solution. I just wanted to make sure this "issue" has been considered, and it looks like you did think about it.

Another thing that just popped into my mind: this feature sounds like it could work nicely with modules.  You can imagine having a few UI elements that are grouped together into a module and wanting to insert that module dynamically.  Has this idea been looked at as well? If it's easy to make them work together, that's awesome.  Though it might not be very easy to support that, I'm not sure.

One last comment: When removing inputs, the user needs to know how to write the exact (sometimes complex) javascript expression to capture the correct element. Have you considered doing something similar to what I do in shinyjs, where I try to automatically detect if the id corresponds to an input or not, which makes it a lot easier to use?  https://github.com/daattali/shinyjs/blob/master/inst/srcjs/shinyjs-default-funcs.js#L48-L57
It's a tadeoff between trying to be helpful and making too many (potentially dangerous?) assumptions.

ui <- fluidPage(
  shinyjs::useShinyjs(),
  uiOutput("selectPlaceholder"),
  actionButton("toggle", "toggle"), br(), br(),

  actionButton("add", "Add UI")
)

# Server logic
server <- function(input, output, session) {
  observeEvent(input$add, {
    insertUI(
      selector = "#add",
      where = "afterEnd",
      ui = textInput(paste0("txt", input$add),

                     paste0("Insert some text ", input$add))
    )
  })

  output$selectPlaceholder <- renderUI({
    inputs <- grep("^txt\\d+$", names(input), value = TRUE)
    selectInput("select", "Select an input to toggle", choices = inputs)
  })

  observeEvent(input$toggle, {
    shinyjs::toggleState(input$select)
  })
}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

> As for the second suggestion, I definitely struggled with that. This <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/insertAdjacentHTML> is what the `where` argument was based off of. I totally understand your intuition and initially felt the same way. However, since `where` is always relative to the `selector`, I don't think there's a very elegant way to add elements after one another, instead of the more stack-like format that `afterEnd` produces. There is a workaround, however, which is to use `beforeEnd` instead -- `beforeEnd` makes newly inserted elements children of the `selector` element, so it's definitely a bad idea to use it is your `selector` is a button or something like that. But if your `selector` is a just a placeholder div, then, this produces the result you intended: `beforeEnd` always adds the new element as the *last* child of the `selector` element, so the visual result is that things get inserted one after another. This is actually why `beforeEnd` is the default. It is also the pattern I use for the demo app <https://beta.rstudioconnect.com/barbara/insertUI/> (use a placeholder as `selector` and stick to the `beforeEnd` default). Maybe I should make this clearer in the documentation or the article. Do you feel like this is enough flexibility for the user?

> > > There’s two new functions: insertUI and removeUI, which allow you to add and remove arbitrary pieces of UI to your app. The best way to familiarize yourself with these might be to check out this demo app <https://beta.rstudioconnect.com/barbara/insertUI/> and read this article <http://shiny.rstudio-staging.com/articles/dynamic-ui.html>.

> > >
> > > I’ll leave you with parts of the documentation and minimal examples:
> > >
> > > insertUI
> > >
> > > This function allows you to dynamically add an arbitrarily large UI object into your app, whenever you want, as many times as you want. Unlike renderUI, the UI generated with insertUI is not updatable as a whole: once it's created, it stays there. Each new call to insertUI creates more UI objects, in addition to the ones already there (all independent from one another). To update a part of the UI (ex: an input object), you must use the appropriate render function or a customized reactive function. To remove any part of your UI, use removeUI.
> > >
> > > Note that whatever UI object you pass through ui, it is always wrapped in an extra div (or if inline = TRUE, a span) before making its way into the DOM. This does not affect what you mean to do, and it makes it easier to remove the whole UI object using removeUI (if you wish to do so, of course).

Hi all I am new here but I have question that is bothering me for long time already, it is related to creation of the PDF's via Shiny and knit r.

I build shiny app that is expected to create PDF report out of the user input data, through knitr. My application is working perfectly when run on my computer through R Studio but once I upload it to the shiny server (shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>) some latex packages that I use stop working and I do not understand why. Using eso-pic or hyperref result in error:
Running ' texi2div ' on ' pdf_shell.tex ' failed.

To solve this problem I tried to use  xelatex compiler when compiling the PDF but it did not solve all of my problems. My problem is mainly related to the hyperref package which is functioning well when run through the R Studio but crash or covers text when run through shiny server. Below you will find pictures visualizing my problem with hyperref (one is compiled through R Studio (working well) and the "broken" via deployed app on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>).
Does anyone know how I could compile the PDF using default compiler pdflatex, without getting the above mentioned error? Or you maybe have any pro tips that could solve the problems differently. Any input is much appreciated.

I compile documents via shiny simply with:
output$report = downloadHandler(
filename = reactive({paste0(input$filename,'.pdf')}),

content = function(file) {
out = knit2pdf(input = 'pdf_shell.Rnw')
 file.rename(out, file)
 },

contentType = 'application/pdf' )

Thank you,
Wiktor

messages.subject: Announcement: ShinyDevCon videos now available
messages.subject_clean: Announcement: ShinyDevCon videos now available
messages.body_plain:
(Repost from https://blog.rstudio.org/2016/05/05/shinydevcon-videos-now-available/)

This past January, we held the first ever Shiny Developer Conference. It was a chance to gather together a group of intermediate to advanced Shiny users, and take their skills to the next level.

It was an exciting event for me in particular, as I’ve been dying to share some of these intermediate and advanced Shiny concepts for years now. There are many concepts that aren’t strictly required to be productive with Shiny, but make a huge difference in helping you write efficient, robust, maintainable apps—and also make Shiny app authoring a lot more satisfying.

The feedback we received from conference attendees was overwhelmingly positive: everyone from relative novices to the most advanced users told us they gained new insights into how to improve their Shiny apps, or had a perspective shift on concepts they thought they already understood. The user-contributed lightning talks were also a big hit, helping people see what’s possible using Shiny and inspiring them to push their own apps further.

If you weren’t able to attend but are still interested in building your Shiny skills, we’re happy to announce the availability of videos of the tutorials and talks:

Shiny Developer Conference 2016 Videos <https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/>

At the moment, these videos are our best sources of info on the topics of reactive programming, Shiny gadgets, Shiny modules, debugging Shiny apps, and performance. If you’re at all serious about writing Shiny apps, we highly recommend you take the time to watch!

If you’re interested in attending next year’s conference, you can sign up for our email list using the subscription form at the top of the Shiny Developer Conference 2016 Videos <https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/> page, and we’ll let you know when more details are available.

A reactive expression/conductor, or
An observer
This may feel like a limitation but it's actually a feature--as in almost 100% of cases, if you're trying to read a reactive expression or value from outside one of those contexts, it's because of a misunderstanding of reactive programming.

In your example:

  if (myconductor()$c){
    output$component <- renderText(paste(myconductor()$a, collapse=','))
  } else {
    output$component <- renderText(paste(myconductor()$b, collapse=','))
  }

The value of myconductor() will change over time--this is the nature of reactive expressions. But this code will run only once. Instead, you need to invert the logic to this:

output$component <- renderText({
  if (myconductor()$c) {
    paste(myconductor()$a, collapse=",")
  } else {
    paste(myconductor()$b, collapse=",")
  }
})

Don't think of assignment to output$whatever as saying "update the value of this output to xxx", but rather, "here is the RECIPE for how you would update the output, I'll let you (the framework) worry about when and how often to actually perform the update".

I highly recommend that you work through the "Effective reactive programming" videos here: https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/shiny-developer-conference/ At the very least, you will find Part 1 very helpful I think.

messages.subject: Re: Announcement: insertUI and removeUI functions now available on Shiny's development version
messages.subject_clean: Announcement: insertUI and removeUI functions now available on Shiny's development version
messages.body_plain:
Yes, this is a bit of a different type of demo app than we have done in the past. In this case, the actual code displayed with showcase mode is not particularly helpful or meant to be analyzed by the average user (so it is not supposed to be a demo of <<- at all; that's just what I'm using behind-ish the scenes). That's what the panels on the left are for. I added the `ui.R` part now, to make it really clear that's all you're supposed to use for the insertUI and removeUI functionality. The actual code is there just because 1) we've got into the habit of making all demo apps in showcase mode; 2) to satisfy the curiosity of the more advanced users.

I'll also try to make a modules example, I hadn't really considered that so far. Thanks the idea!

@ MySchizoBuddy, for an explanation of the `where` part, I think checking out this fiddle <https://fiddle.jshell.net/46unexjx/> I created may the best way to get it. You may also want to take a look at this link <https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Element/insertAdjacentHTML> (`position` argument). We don't use that particular function itself, but that's what the `where` argument is based off of.

@ Dean Attali, yes, needing to know the precise javascript expression when removing UI objects is a bummer... But I felt a little uneasy about making dangerous assumptions, as you said, so I left it at that. I'll look at your code and see if I can find some middle ground.

Thanks for your suggestions!
Barbara

Modules would be inserted like this:

observeEvent(input$addModuleButton, {
  callModule(mymodule, "some_id", ...)
  insertUI("body", "beforeEnd",
    mymoduleUI("some_id", ...)
  )
})

i.e. call callModule in addition to inserting the module UI.

messages.subject_clean: Best practice for integrating d3 with fine-tuned control in Shiny?
messages.body_plain:
You might be able to do this with callback functions, using the htmlwidgets::onRender function--see the reference documentation of that function for more details.

library(networkD3)
data(MisLinks, MisNodes)
forceNetwork(Links = MisLinks, Nodes = MisNodes, Source = "source",
             Target = "target", Value = "value", NodeID = "name",
             Group = "group", opacity = 0.4) %>%
  onRender("function(el, x) {
    ...
  }")

The value of "x" in the JS code is highly dependent on the htmlwidget binding code; in the case of the networkD3::forceNetwork function, it's the d3.layout.force() object.

With the GitHub version of htmlwidgets (i.e. not yet released on CRAN) you can pass an additional argument such as a list or data frame to onRender, and that will be made available to your JS code as well.

Not really a Shiny question, but, I'd work around it by using do.call instead of calling testFunc directly. do.call(testFunc, list(x = model, pred.data = dataSet, x.var = var, plot = F))

Alternatively, use this approach: http://adv-r.had.co.nz/Computing-on-the-language.html#substitute

Incidentally, partialPlot has a bug: its eval() should be passing in the parent frame of the partialPlot call. The way it's written, it'll basically only evaluate in the global environment, which is why it wasn't working for you in the lapply. If you're not actually using partialPlot but implementing something similar, consider using the lazyeval approach instead, which is way more sane: https://github.com/hadley/lazyeval/blob/master/vignettes/lazyeval.Rmd

messages.subject: Re: intermediate action button necessary to update graph-not responding
messages.subject_clean: intermediate action button necessary to update graph-not responding
messages.body_plain:
Hi Chris,

you don't need to implement a two-step update process. Actually, you could also have the graph redraw immediately once some checkboxes change, unless it was your intention to make updates only on demand, e.g. because of lengthy computations.

In order to implement the update button don't use calls to `isolate` and `observeEvent`; rather use `eventReactive` to create an reactive expression which is triggered by the button click. You can than use it in your plotting function similarly as you tried before:

#ui.R
checkboxGroupInput("column_choices", "column choice", colnames(data), selected=c("column1", "column2"....)),

actionButton(inputId="button", label="Update plot"),
plotOutput("graph")

#server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output) {
  dataInput <- eventReactive(input$button, {
    tagData(IRIS[, input$column_choices])
  })
  output$graph <- renderPlot({
    package_defined_plot_function(data=data, dataTag=dataInput()))
    })
})

See also "Pattern 2 - Delay reactions" at http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/action-buttons.html

"actionbutton B" will then update the graph with the new input from the preliminary processing command.

messages.subject: shiny giving spurious data-analysis output in comparison to non-shiny environment
messages.subject_clean: shiny giving spurious data-analysis output in comparison to non-shiny environment
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to implement some analysis in a shiny app via a package-defined command that outputs a plot. This package defined command requires preliminary input from a separate command (one that specifies which specific columns in a given data matrix are to be assessed- these columns contain information about cell types).
#ui.R
uiactual <- dashboardPage(
  dashboardHeader(title="Project"),
   [dashboard sidebar....]
  dashboardBody(tabItems(
        box(sliderInput(inputId="maximum_genes", label="Choose number genes per cell-type", value=15, min=5, max=15)),
        column(7, checkboxGroupInput("cell_choices", "choose cell types", colnames(IRIS), selected=c("Bcell-naïve", "CD4Tcell-N0","Monocyte-Day0", "NKcell-control", "Neutrophil-Resting"))),
        actionButton(inputId="choices", label="Update heatmap"),
        column(12,plotOutput("graph"))
       )
  )
 )
)

 #server.R
 serveractual <- function(input, output) {
     dataInput<-eventReactive(input$choices, {
     tagData(IRIS[, input$cell_choices], max=input$maximum_genes)
     })
 output$graph<-renderPlot({
    package_defined_plot( data=data, dataTag=dataInput() )
    })
 }

See in the above code for server.R, the tagData command is the preliminary process that is required for output from package_defined_plot.

The point of this analysis is to check visually and numerically for a significant difference between the column specified cell types.

While the mechanism of analysis seems in no way impaired, for some reason the input (stored in function dataInput) is perturbed such that the output is completely different from what would be expected in a non-shiny environment. See below the significance values that accompany the heat maps that are output:

 <http://i.stack.imgur.com/DTlGx.png>

Above is the normal significance obtained for each cell type.

 <http://i.stack.imgur.com/HXPRp.png>

Notice the different significance values across the cell types when implemented in shiny.

Because of this the output heat maps are wrong when processed in shiny.

The shiny output is normal when I omit the dataInput function and just give the dataTag argument as normal. Hence, for some reason the transfer of information through the dataInput function is not delivering the input information properly.

To see if this was due to the checkboxgroupInput that goes into dataInput(), gave the dataInput()normal arguments- but the same incorrect output still resulted.

Overall there is something wrong with the way that I am storing column-specific information within the shiny implemented dataInput(). While the output in shiny is consistent after multiple testing (i.e. it doesn't just randomly change), it is wrong.

Can anyone tell me how I might rectify this?

messages.subject_clean: extracting values from leaflet::addDrawToolbar function
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I have installed the development version of leaflet so I can use some of the leaflet.draw plugin functionalities. My end goal is to allow a user of my Shiny app to draw a custom polygon on the leaflet map. From which, I can use the polygon coordinates to subset spatial data.

My specific question concerns the addDrawToolbar() function: How do I extract the coordinates of user created objects from the returned value of addDrawToolbar()?

I am using the following code in a shiny implementation and --as suggested in the function documentation-- am trying to extract the coordinates using input$drawnItems_create[[3]]$coordinates. Clearly, I'm not following the proper usage because I only get a NULL value returned. Here's my code:
devtools::install_github("byzheng/leaflet")
library(shiny)
library(leaflet)

shinyUI(bootstrapPage(
  tags$style(type = "text/css", "html, body {width:100%;height:100%}"),
  leafletOutput("map", width = "100%", height = "100%"),
  absolutePanel(top = 80, right = 10, width = 200,
                actionButton("drawPoints", "Draw polygon")
  )
))

shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  output$map <- renderLeaflet({
    addTiles(leaflet())
  })

  # User draws polygon
  observeEvent(input$drawPoints, {
    leafletProxy("map") %>%
      addDrawToolbar()
    print(input$drawnItems_create[[3]]$coordinates) # this returns NULL
  })
})

Any suggestions or assistance would be appreciated. Thank you,

Matt Schumwinger

messages.body_plain:
I read through the Shiny code and fluidPage (which calls bootstrapPage, etc.) doesn't seem to do anything to handle a NULL title.  It seems it's just regular behavior in browsers to have the window title default to the URL if the HTML document itself does not contain a title (which isn't strictly valid HTML I think).

Note that I also tried to see if head tag "hoisting" (as mentioned by Joe Cheng here: https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/issues/22 ) would work.  e.g.:
 tags$head( tags$title('A page by any other name would be as lame') )

I couldn't seem to get the title to be "hoisted".

Nevertheless, it still seems as though it's at least theoretically possible to modify the title of the generated HTML document from within the shinyServer function.

Any ideas?

> It's interesting that for a fluidPage, the title, if left unspecified, defaults to the host URL of the page.  However, what I'd like to do is derive a page title *from* the host URL of the page, but not have it be exactly equal to the host URL.
>
> So, I guess the question is:  How can I access the host URL of the page outside of the shinyServer function which receives the session variable (which contains clientData and the url_* components)?  (Apparently "fluidPage" is able to do that somehow.)

messages.subject: Re: Shiny Server URL
messages.subject_clean: Shiny Server URL
messages.body_plain:
Port 3838 is the (default) port that Shiny Server listens on. Shiny Server then launches multiple R processes to run the actual Shiny apps; these also need ports to listen on, and they can't be 3838 as it is taken by Shiny Server. So they listen on random ports chosen by Shiny Server. However, these ports can only be accessed from localhost, and furthermore a "shared secret" is passed from Shiny Server to each Shiny process so that no other processes can perform requests against those random ports.

Please configure your firewall not to block ports on 127.0.0.1, and it should work.

messages.subject: Shiny + Leaflet Bottlenecks
messages.subject_clean: Shiny + Leaflet Bottlenecks
messages.body_plain:
This is a pretty high-level question, so not sure if there is an appropriate answer...

I've been building some Shiny+Leaflet mapping apps for my job. Thus far, I've been limiting the # of points I'm plotting in order for the app to run smoothly and be responsive. In a few instances, I've tried to scale up to hundreds of thousands of points and see the dramatic slow down.

I'm beginning to get interest from company higher-ups in developing these apps further. I was wondering if anyone here could tell me what they know about what bottlenecks a Shiny leaflet app? I was thinking of doing a Proof of Concept using a dedicated Shiny server with a beefy amount of RAM and processing power (relative to my dinky laptop), but wanted to know what to expect in terms of scaling and bottlenecks. I'm not an experience software developer so excuse me if I'm using incorrect terminology.

messages.subject: Re: Shiny + Leaflet Bottlenecks
messages.subject_clean: Shiny + Leaflet Bottlenecks
messages.body_plain:
Hey Malcolm, first of all congrats - that's an exciting stage of a project.

You are going to have serious bottlenecks when trying to show tens of thousands of points let alone "hundreds of thousands of points" with Leaflet or OpenLayers, etc (not due to R RStudio/leaflet or your server). It will be worse once you put it on a server because then it will have to transmit the data to the client (which is actually a worse bottleneck ...). However, you have many options and I'll highlight only a few (I'm going to assume the styling needs to change based on R calculations or user inputs):

Stick with what you have:
only show what is within map_bounds (could be slow data transmission)
Yelp-style click to analyze new region and then show points (might not be good UI design ...)
marker clustering
depending on the zoom level, aggregate to an appropriate jurisdictional boundary (zip+4, county, etc)
Add Geoserver:
set up GeoServer on the same server and use a pre-existing shapefile of points (or host using PostGIS). You will need to send custom styling from the app to Geoserver which still won't be perfect. I'd be happy to help with this off-line.
Ditch it all:
If none of these solutions do the trick (and your users have WebGL enabled browsers) you may have to jump ship: https://github.com/mapbox/mapbox-gl-js
Chris

Yelp-click will just be an actionButton tied to a reactive that does a gBuffer + gIntersection (sp object) from the subsequent map_click. I'm sure the framework will work for you but you may have to add on other tools - it's certainly worked for us. Joe, hexbinning is cool, and FWIW Cartodb has open-sourced their PostGIS extensions including that capability: https://github.com/CartoDB/cartodb-postgresql/blob/224b2ce39504f974cc47602fd49c3fecb60a5b27/scripts-available/CDB_Hexagon.sql. While we are the topic of showing/sending a lot of data, I'm wondering if this would help: https://github.com/rstudio/leaflet/issues/237.

Chris

messages.subject_clean: fetch new data from googlesheet on actionbutton
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I am trying to wire up an action button on my ui.R for the user to fire it up in order to fetch new data from a googlesheet and then use that data in the entire app. Each time this button is fired, all of the formulas and functions should be recalculated based on this new data.

library(shiny)
library(leaflet)
library(googlesheets)
shinyServer(function(input, output, session) {

  fetcheddata <- reactive({
    mybutton <- input$fetchnew
    if (is.null(mybutton)) return (NULL)
    mydata <- gs_read(gs_key("abcdefghijkabcdefghijkabcdefghijkabcdefghijk"))
    mydata$latitude <- as.numeric(ptsdata$latitude)
    mydata$longitude <- as.numeric(ptsdata$longitude)
    mydata
  })
  output$draw <- renderTable(
    fetcheddata()
   )

and on the ui.R side, I have a line for the button:

actionButton("fetchnew", "Fetch New Data")

why am I doing this? because when new data is added to the speadsheet, they don't show up on the running shiny app session. I have to wait for that session to go to sleep and then run the app to see the new data.

My app is based on the superzip shiny app, so there is another reactive expressions afterwards.
I need the community's suggestions to set this up.
thank you in advance

messages.subject: Shinyapps.io: Worker-Connection ID available?
messages.subject_clean: Shinyapps.io: Worker-Connection ID available?
messages.body_plain:
I want to build an app that will be hosted on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> that writes to an external database. Since there could be multiple instances containing multiple  workers which have multiple connections, creating a unique record ID to write to the database is a challenge.

The main part of the challenge is an environment variable that increments with each write request could theoretically be duplicated in a simultaneously running instance / worker / connection.

One way to do it would be to have access to the unique connection ID, if there is such a thing.

I realise that some database implementations can force a unique ID, but for various reasons I want to be able to keep ID generation within the app. Clearly system time, user ID and an incremented variable could provide a solution that will *almost* always provide a unique combination, but to be absolutely watertight, a reference to the worker-connection instance would be necessary. Is this something a shiny app hosted in shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> can access?

Or is there a way that anybody can think of to generate guaranteed unique IDs between two simultaneous R processes where the user and time stamp could, theoretically, be identical.

messages.subject: Re: Using packages not on CRAN in shiny
messages.subject_clean: Using packages not on CRAN in shiny
messages.body_plain:
Sorry, packages must be on CRAN, BioConductor, R-forge (I think), or GitHub for us to be able to find them. The problem is that we need to reinstall the package from source to work on our Linux servers, and only those three specific types of repositories are supported by the tools we use (devtools and packrat).

I think other people have hit this issue before, you could try installing from this repo:

devtools::install_github("andrewzm/INLA")

It looks like it's from about six months ago. Alternatively, you could create your own GitHub repository and host the contents of the package source tarball there.

Sorry, I'm sure those aren't very satisfying answers...

messages.subject: Re: Announcement: insertUI and removeUI functions now available on Shiny's development version
messages.subject_clean: Announcement: insertUI and removeUI functions now available on Shiny's development version
messages.body_plain:
A few updates:
I changed the demo app <https://gallery.shinyapps.io/insertUI/> to `DisplayMode: Normal`; hopefully this eliminates the confusion of having code that does not directly pertain to the insertUI/removeUI functionality.
I've created two other apps (both of these *are* in Showcase mode, but I believe should not be confusing as they're very simple) -- both of these are linked to from the article <http://shiny.rstudio-staging.com/articles/dynamic-ui.html>:
queue demo <https://gallery.shinyapps.io/111-insert-ui/>: using insertUI/removeUI to insert and delete text elements following a queue logic;
modules demo <https://gallery.shinyapps.io/insertUI-modules/>: using insertUI to dynamically add modules (note that each module's plots can be brushed independently from one another).
We've decided not to try to "guess" the selector for the removeUI function, partly because it can be dangerous, and partly because we want to allow the user to remove anything within the page, not just Shiny-specific objects. Our current recommendation is that you wrap your insertUI's `ui` in a `tags$div` and provide an id to that div, which makes it trivial to remove it later on using removeUI (if your div's id is "mydiv", to remove it, you'd do: `removeUI( selector = "#mydiv" )`. )

messages.subject_clean: Shiny Modules: how to access the input$ of a looped Shiny Module?
messages.body_plain:
I think I realized what Mark is trying to accomplish, i had similar idea prior to shiny module becoming available.
below are modified code based on the above gist that allows user to do filtering more freely.

library(shiny)

dynamicSelectInput <- function(id, label, multiple = FALSE){

  ns <- shiny::NS(id)

  shiny::selectInput(ns("dynamic_select"), label,
                     choices = NULL, multiple = multiple, width = "100%")

}

#' Dynamical Update of a selectInput
#' @param the_data data.frame containing column of choices
#' @param column The column to select from
#' @param default_select The choices to select on load
dynamicSelect <- function(input, output, session, the_data, column, default_select = NULL){

  ## update input$dynamic_select
  observe({
    shiny::validate(
      shiny::need(the_data(),"Fetching data")
    )
    dt <- the_data()

    testthat::expect_is(dt, "data.frame")
    testthat::expect_is(column, "character")

    choice <- unique(dt[[column]])

    updateSelectInput(session, "dynamic_select",
                      choices = choice,
                      selected = default_select)

  })

  return(reactive(input$dynamic_select))

}

#' Using Dynamic Input
#' @param id Shiny Id
#' @param aggs The Aggregation names
outerTableUI <- function(id, aggs){

  ns <- shiny::NS(id)

  tagList(
    fluidRow(
      lapply(seq_along(aggs), function(x) {
        column(width = 4,
               dynamicSelectInput(ns(aggs[[x]]), aggs[[x]], multiple = TRUE)
        )

      })
    ),
    fluidRow(
      ## if this works should be able to filter this table
      ## by the selected filters above
      tableOutput(ns("table"))
    )

  )
}

#' server side
#' @export
outerTable <- function(input, output, session, the_data, aggs){

  selectResults <- lapply(setNames(aggs, aggs), function(agg) {
    callModule(module = dynamicSelect,
               id = agg,
               the_data = the_data,
               column = agg)
  })

  new_data <- reactive({
    old_data <- the_data()

    new_data <- NULL
    for(i in seq_along(aggs)){

      agg <- aggs[i]

      if(is.null(inputA <- selectResults[[agg]]())){
        next
      } else{
        old_col <- old_data[[agg]]

        new_data <- old_data[old_col %in% inputA,]

        old_data <- new_data
      }

    }

    new_data

  })

  output$table <- renderTable({
    # browser()
    new_data()
  })

}

### Call via:

the_data <- mtcars
the_filters = names(mtcars)

shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    outerTableUI("debug_dynamic",
                 aggs = the_filters)
  ),
  server = function(input, output, session){
    callModule(outerTable,
               "debug_dynamic",
               the_data = reactive(the_data),
               aggs = the_filters)
  }
)

messages.subject_clean: Shiny reset everything to default when click on shinyFile's shinyDirButton button.
messages.body_plain:
While building a shiny app, there is a button to choose directory of files this button made by shinyFiles package. There are also some radio buttons on page or a button to show/hide **Hide data chunk** a div. Problem is after first time select the folder, then select any other radio button which was not default or click on show/hide button it becomes **Show data chunk**, then as soon as second time click on **choose directory** button it reset radio button to default selected and change the value of show/hide button to default which was at first time load page. Why it reset these elements by click on second time to folder select? Here is the code. **ui.R** library(shiny) library(shinyFiles) library(shinyjs) shinyUI(fluidPage( titlePanel("Data Insights"), sidebarPanel( useShinyjs(), shinyDirButton('directory', 'Folder select', 'Please select a folder'), tags$div(id = "DrawChartFiltersWraper", uiOutput("chartsTypeControls") ), ), mainPanel( uiOutput('allStats'), tags$br(), uiOutput('dataChunkHeading') ), )) **server.R** shinyServer(function(input, output, session) { # make data frame from CSV files. dataFrame <- reactive({ volumes <- getVolumes() shinyDirChoose(input, 'directory', roots=volumes, session=session, restrictions=system.file(package='base')) validate ( need(input$directory != "", "<< Please select a CSV folder"), errorClass = "missing-folder" ) getDataFrame(parseDirPath(volumes, input$directory)) }) output$chartsTypeControls <- renderUI({ chartTypes <- c("Bar Chart", "Pie Chart", "Scatterplot") radioButtons("chartTypes", "Choose Chart Type", chartTypes) }) # data Chunk output$dataChunkHeading <- renderUI({ toggleDataChunk <- actionButton("toggleDataChunk", "Hide data chunk", class = "btn-primary") HTML(paste("

Data chunk of provided data.

", toggleDataChunk)) }) output$allStats <- renderUI({ total_rows = nrow(dataFrame) total_columns = ncol(dataFrame) overAllTxt <- paste('

Overall Insights


', "Total Rows:", total_rows, "Total Columns:", total_columns, "

") HTML(overAllTxt) }) })

> library(shiny)
>
> dynamicSelectInput <- function(id, label, multiple = FALSE){
>
>   ns <- shiny::NS(id)
>
>   shiny::selectInput(ns("dynamic_select"), label,
>                      choices = NULL, multiple = multiple, width = "100%")
>
> }
>
> #' Dynamical Update of a selectInput
> #' @param the_data data.frame containing column of choices
> #' @param column The column to select from
> #' @param default_select The choices to select on load
> dynamicSelect <- function(input, output, session, the_data, column, default_select = NULL){
>
>   ## update input$dynamic_select
>   observe({
>     shiny::validate(
>       shiny::need(the_data(),"Fetching data")
>     )
>     dt <- the_data()
>
>     testthat::expect_is(dt, "data.frame")
>     testthat::expect_is(column, "character")
>
>     choice <- unique(dt[[column]])
>
>     updateSelectInput(session, "dynamic_select",
>                       choices = choice,
>                       selected = default_select)
>
>   })
>
>   return(reactive(input$dynamic_select))
>
> }
>
> #' Using Dynamic Input
> #' @param id Shiny Id
> #' @param aggs The Aggregation names
> outerTableUI <- function(id, aggs){
>
>   ns <- shiny::NS(id)
>
>   tagList(
>     fluidRow(
>       lapply(seq_along(aggs), function(x) {
>         column(width = 4,
>                dynamicSelectInput(ns(aggs[[x]]), aggs[[x]], multiple = TRUE)
>         )
>
>       })
>     ),

>     )
>

> }

>   })
>
>
> }
>
>

>

>   ui = fluidPage(
>     outerTableUI("debug_dynamic",
>                  aggs = the_filters)

messages.subject: Using R6 objects to share objects between sessions via the global.R
messages.subject_clean: Using R6 objects to share objects between sessions via the global.R
messages.body_plain:
So, I was playing around with R6 classes in shiny, and realized that I could use them to pass info between shiny sessions on the same app

I'm curious though:

How reliable/safe is this? where is the object actually stored? is there a risk that these shared objects (on say, shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io>) could be used by user to store large amounts of arbitrary stuff on the server?

Example:

The idea is, if we have a shared object, that each server is an instance of, they can all effect a shared repository of data, so instead of doing all our coding in the server.R file, we do it in the global.R

The neat thing is, this allows people to actually communicate with one another between shiny sessions on the same app.

Example:

global.R
library(R6)
library(shiny)

# Create a Server Object that has a method 'run' that is called by the server
# file. This allows the method to have access to internal objects, thus, each
# each instance of a shiny application can access the same shared objects as
# every other instance of that run function (since they all can effect the
# same class object

server <- R6Class(
  classname = 'server',
  public = list(
  # sharedObject is what we will pass between sessions.
  sharedObject = list(),
  initialize = function() {
  },
  run = function(input, output, session) {
    output$CalcOutput <- renderText({
     self$sharedObject <- input$number
     input$number
   })
   output$CalcOutput2 <- renderText({
     input$Friends
     self$output
   })
  }
 )
)

# Create the object, everyone shares this.
channel <- server$new()

ui.R
 library(shiny)
 fluidPage(
   numericInput('number','Number',100000000),
   textOutput('CalcOutput'),
   actionButton('Friends','Whats My Friends Num?'),
   textOutput('CalcOutput2')
 )

server.R
# Now, each instance will be
channel$run

Load up 2 copies of the app (either on your server, or through a browser)

change the number on one of the two apps, and then press the button to check it on the other app, you'll find that it's changed.

messages.subject: How to store/retrieve input field values to/from different reactive based upon master input field
messages.subject_clean: How to store/retrieve input field values to/from different reactive based upon master input field
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I want to create a UI with several slave input fields (mostly textInput and selectInput fields) and store their value in different reactive objects depending on the value of a master selectInput field. Practically, if the value of the master selectInput field is, let's say, 'a', I want to store all other slave field values to the slot "a" of a list of reactives; if the master selectInput field is "b", the slave field values are store in the slot "b" of the same list. The overall goal is to allow users to switch from one selection to another in the master selectInput field and retrieve the information they provided earlier, rather than resetting all slave fields to default.

I thought using eventReactive would be the way to go, but either this is not the right approach or my event conditions are wrong as illustrated in the code below (using a single slave field). Theoretically, I could create as many set of slave inputs as I have possible values in my master selectInput and show/hide them using conditionalPanel functions. However, this is practically not possible in my real app, as the choices in my master selectInput are also defined by a reactive with a priori unknown number of elements and unknown values.

Any suggestions to achieve the overall goal would be greatly appreciated.

Thank you

server <- function(input, output, session){

    output$selector <- renderUI({
        selectInput('dataSelector',
          label = 'Select a data',
          choices = letters[1:3])
      })

    dfs <- letters[1:3]
    names(dfs) <- dfs
    storeText <- sapply(dfs,
      function(x) {
        eventReactive(input$dataSelector==x,
          {input$text})
      },
      USE.NAMES = TRUE
    )

    output$text <- renderUI({
        textInput('text',
          label = 'Enter some text',
          value = storeText[[input$dataSelector]]())
      })

    output$check <- renderPrint({
        cat('Value of input$text')
        print(input$text)
        cat('Value of storeText$a')
        print(storeText$a())
        cat('Value of storeText$b')
        print(storeText$b())
        cat('Value of storeText$c')
        print(storeText$c())
        print(dfs)
        print(storeText)
      })

  })

ui.R <- fluidPage(
    uiOutput('selector'),
    uiOutput('text'),
    verbatimTextOutput('check')
  ))

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

Thanks for the quick response!

The reason I moved away from the Leaflet R package (amazing though it is!) was that it was my understanding that I couldn't get away from the EPSG:3857 projection system leaflet expects -- my goal was to set a ratio of 1:1 pixel to internal lat/lon and zoom a digital image.

Is there a way to set a custom projection in your package that I haven't uncovered?

If not would you mind taking a quick look at the example I have? The custom binding looks to be an extremely powerful concept that I'd like to at least have a base understanding of.

Li Wang

I am not sure whether this is possible or not.
For example say a user enters some number into a reactive function they hit a button which multiplies every cell.
Then when they like those numbers they can hit another button which will send those particular values to a data frame (this data frame being completely non reactive).
In short I am asking, can you make reactive values non reactive? To me this seems like something pretty important.

Here is my code in which I am trying to make tabplot become an unreactive copy.

library(shiny)
library(rhandsontable)

seq1 <- seq(1:6)
mat1 <- matrix(seq1, 2)

tabplot<-data.frame(car=numeric(2),num=numeric(2),truck=numeric(2))

did_recalc <- FALSE

ui <- fluidPage(
  rHandsontableOutput('table'),
  tableOutput('result'),
  textOutput('ca'),
  actionButton("goButton","Confirm"),
  verbatimTextOutput("otest"),
  actionButton("checkButton","Apply"),
  br(),
  actionButton("recalc", "Return to original values")

)

server <- function(input,output,session)({

 # tabplot<-data.frame(car=numeric(2),num=numeric(2),truck=numeric(2))

  seq1 <- seq(1:6)
 # mat1 <- matrix(seq1, 2)

  mat1<- data.frame(x=1:2,y=3:4,z=5:6)

  #creates reactive values for the data frame
  #obviously they have to be reactive values to function with the rhandsontable which is being continuously updated
  #as the documentation says "values taken from the reactiveValues object are reactive but the object itself is not
  values <- reactiveValues(data=mat1)

  #if recalc --- which connects to an action button in the ui is hit, values goes back to original data frame
  observe({
    input$recalc
    values$data<-mat1
  })

  #Where the magic happens
  output$table <- renderRHandsontable({
    rhandsontable(values$data,selectCallback = TRUE)
  })

  #this changes the handsontable format to an r object
  observe({
    if(!is.null(input$table))
      values$data <-hot_to_r(input$table)
  })

  #Here we create a reactive function that creates a data frame of the rhandsontable output but it is a reactive function
  fn<-reactive({
    co<-data.frame((values$data))
    return(co)
  })

  #Bit of testing, this demonstrates that the fn() is only updated after the button is pressed
  output$result<-renderTable({
    input$goButton
    isolate({
      fn()
    })
  })

  #observe({
 #   if(!is.null(input$table))
 #     values$data <-hot_to_r(input$table)
 # })

 # observe({
   # if(did_recalc = FALSE)
#  tabplot<-reactive({                              #Format co[desired row:length(colums)][desired column]

  #observeEvent(input$checkButton,{

    isolate({
      tabplot[1,1:3][1]<-fn()[1,1:3][1]
      tabplot[1,1:3][2]<-fn()[1,1:3][2]
      tabplot[1,1:3][3]<-fn()[1,1:3][3]

      tabplot[2,1:3][1]<-fn()[2,1:3][1]
      tabplot[2,1:3][2]<-fn()[2,1:3][2]
      tabplot[2,1:3][3]<-fn()[2,1:3][3]

    })

  observe({
    input$checkButton
    output$ca<-renderText({
      tabplot$car
      cat('\nAccessing Subset with $:', tabplot$car)
      cat('\nAccessing specific cell:',tabplot[1,3])
      cat('\nAccessing specific cell:',tabplot[[1]])
      cat('\noperations on specific cell:',tabplot[1,3]*2)
    })
  })

})
shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

messages.subject: Conflict between Shiny bootstrap web dependency and wrapbootstrap theme
messages.subject_clean: Conflict between Shiny bootstrap web dependency and wrapbootstrap theme
messages.body_plain:
Also posted on StackExchange....

I am building a Shiny web app (eventually to be deployed using Shiny Server) and I downloaded the Ambrosia web app theme from wrapbootstrap (https://wrapbootstrap.com/theme/ambrosia-web-application-theme-WB06SM719) to style the page. The local prototype of the home page is implemented as follows:

library(shiny)

ui <- fluidPage(suppressDepencies("bootstrap"),
    tags$head(
        tags$meta(name="description",content=""),
        tags$meta(name="viewport",content="width=device-width"),
        tags$link(rel="stylesheet",href="assets/styles/css/ambrosiabootstrap.min.css"),
        tags$link(rel="stylesheet", href="assets/font-awesome/css/ambrosia-font-awesome.css"),
        tags$link(rel="stylesheet", href="assets/styles/css/ambrosiastyle.css"),
        tags$script(src="assets/js/jquery-1.8.0.min.js"),
        tags$script(src="$.noConflict(true);"),
        tags$script(src="assets/js/bootstrap.min.js")),

    tags$body(
        tags$div(class="navbar navbar-default navbar-fixed-top",role="navigation",
            tags$div(class="container",
                 #Etc.
            )
        )
    )

server <- function(input,output) {}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

Notice that the Shiny bootstrap theme is suppressed - without this step the UI does not render properly and dynamic elements such as dropdown menus do not function. This solution is fine when there are no Shiny HTML widgets required in the UI and the server function is empty (i.e. no R calculations are taking place; the web page is just a simple HTML page rendered via Shiny using the Ambrosia style). However, conflicts arise when I add Shiny widgets and calculations to the server function. For example:
library(shiny)
library(plotly)

ui <- tags$head(<same as before except Shiny bootstrap is not suppressed>)
    tags$body(
       tags$div(class="navbar navbar-default navbar-fixed-top",role="navigation",
            tags$div(class="container",
                 #Etc.
            )
        )
       tags$div(class="container",
           tags$div(class="row",
               tags$div(class="col-lg-8",
                   dataTableOutput("table"),
                   plotlyOutput("plot)",
               )
           )
       )
    )

server <- function(input,output) {

    x <- rnorm(50),
    y <- rnorm(50),
    dat <- data.table(x,y),
    names(dat) <- c("x","y"),

    output$table <- renderDataTable(dat),
    output$plot <- renderPlotly({
        datplot <- plot_ly(dat,x=x,y=y,title="Plot",shape=list(spline))
    })

}

shinyApp(ui = ui, server = server)

This scenario will correctly render the datatable and plotly graph, but the Ambrosia UI is messed up (text in wrong location, dynamic elements not functioning, etc.). If I restore the suppressDepencies("bootstrap") command, the UI is restored but none of the Shiny/plotly elements render. I have tried using a compiled Less CSS file to apply Ambrosia styling only to certain elements in the UI without success. Any ideas on how to resolve this conflict?

For reference, Shiny loads the following command in the tags$head() section when bootstrap is not suppressed:

<script type="application/html-dependencies">json2[2014.02.04];jquery[1.11.3];shiny[0.13.2];**bootstrap[9999]**;datatables[1.10.5];datatables-bootstrap[1.10.5];htmlwidgets[0.6];plotlyjs[1.6.1];plotly-binding[3.4.1]</script><script src="shared/json2-min.js"></script>

When suppressed, it looks like this:

<script type="application/html-dependencies">json2[2014.02.04];jquery[1.11.3];shiny[0.13.2];datatables[1.10.5];datatables-bootstrap[1.10.5];htmlwidgets[0.6];plotlyjs[1.6.1];plotly-binding[3.4.1];bootstrap[3.3.5]</script><script src="shared/json2-min.js"></script>

> Hi shiny folks,
>
> I’m a recent addition to the Shiny team at RStudio and I wanted to let you all know that we’ve just added a pretty exciting new feature to Shiny’s development version (install it with: devtools::install_github("rstudio/shiny”)).
>
> There’s two new functions: insertUI and removeUI, which allow you to add and remove arbitrary pieces of UI to your app. The best way to familiarize yourself with these might be to check out this demo app <https://beta.rstudioconnect.com/barbara/insertUI/> and read this article <http://shiny.rstudio-staging.com/articles/dynamic-ui.html>.
>
> We’re guessing that a lot of you might find this feature useful, so we’d really appreciate if you could try it out and lets us know if you encounter any problems (or just general feedback). We’re hoping to release to CRAN in the coming weeks.
>
>
> I’ll leave you with parts of the documentation and minimal examples:
>
> insertUI
>
> This function allows you to dynamically add an arbitrarily large UI object into your app, whenever you want, as many times as you want. Unlike renderUI, the UI generated with insertUI is not updatable as a whole: once it's created, it stays there. Each new call to insertUI creates more UI objects, in addition to the ones already there (all independent from one another). To update a part of the UI (ex: an input object), you must use the appropriate render function or a customized reactive function. To remove any part of your UI, use removeUI.
>
> Note that whatever UI object you pass through ui, it is always wrapped in an extra div (or if inline = TRUE, a span) before making its way into the DOM. This does not affect what you mean to do, and it makes it easier to remove the whole UI object using removeUI (if you wish to do so, of course).
>
> Example:
>
> ## Only run this example in interactive R sessions
> if (interactive()) {
> # Define UI
> ui <- fluidPage(
>   actionButton("add", "Add UI")
> )
>
> # Server logic
> server <- function(input, output, session) {
>   observeEvent(input$add, {
>     insertUI(
>       selector = "#add",
>       where = "afterEnd",
>       ui = textInput(paste0("txt", input$add),
>                      "Insert some text")
>     )
>   })
> }
>
> # Complete app with UI and server components
> shinyApp(ui, server)
> }
>
>
> removeUI
>
> This function allows you to remove any part of your UI. Once removeUI is executed on some element, it is gone forever. While it may be a particularly useful pattern to pair this with insertUI (to remove some UI you had previously inserted), there is no restriction on what you can use removeUI on. Any element that can be selected through a jQuery selector can be removed through this function.
>
> Example:
>
> ## Only run this example in interactive R sessions
> if (interactive()) {
> # Define UI
> ui <- fluidPage(
>   actionButton("rmv", "Remove UI"),
>   textInput("txt", "This is no longer useful")
> )
>
> # Server logic
> server <- function(input, output, session) {
>   observeEvent(input$rmv, {
>     removeUI(
>       selector = "div:has(> #txt)"
>     )
>   })
> }
>
> # Complete app with UI and server components
> shinyApp(ui, server)
> }
>

messages.subject: Re: Conflict between Shiny bootstrap web dependency and wrapbootstrap theme
messages.subject_clean: Conflict between Shiny bootstrap web dependency and wrapbootstrap theme
messages.body_plain:
Leave off these two lines:

        tags$script(src="assets/js/jquery-1.8.0.min.js"),
        tags$script(src="$.noConflict(true);"),

Instead of loading their older version of jQuery, let Shiny load its version instead. If they were using a newer version then you could consider using their version and doing suppressDependencies("jquery").

>     tags$head(

This solution is fine when there are no Shiny HTML widgets required in the UI and the server function is empty (i.e. no R calculations are taking place; the web page is just a simple HTML page rendered via Shiny using the Ambrosia style). messages.subject: Re: Show Which Accounts Are Currently Connected to Shiny Apps
messages.subject_clean: Show Which Accounts Are Currently Connected to Shiny Apps
messages.body_plain:
There's not a great way to do this on ShinyApps.io, only because by default it runs your app on potentially multiple machines/processes. If all the users were connecting to one process on one machine then you could easily keep a reactiveValues object with global scope (e.g. in server.R but above the shiny server function itself). Then in the shiny server function you could add session$user to the shared object, and use session$onSessionEnded (see ?session) to remove that session$user from the shared object.

http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scoping.html
http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/permissions.html

messages.subject: Queue of Processes
messages.subject_clean: Queue of Processes
messages.body_plain:
I'm working on a Shiny server that processes large datasets and emails results. We've written code to compute and mail the results, but we would like to implement a queuing system to process each submission in the order received.

I plan on utilizing the Queue class described here: http://www.r-bloggers.com/implementing-a-queue-as-a-reference-class/

Currently our flow works like this:

1. A person will input a CSV file and their email into our shiny app.

2. The startServer file observes the submit button, and makes calls to a plotting method (in plotting.R), which plots the data as a PNG, and returns the filename.

3. The returned filename and email are then passed by shinyServer to the mailing method (in mail.R) which mails out the data.

Note: the calls to mail and plotting are not set as "local=TRUE", thus they are in the global environment.

My idea is to:

1. Declare a Queue object (q) outside of the startServer method but still in server.R and call q$push(inputtedData, email).

2. From there, the queue object would make the calls to compute and mail the file to the client, and wait until each job is done before moving onto the next.

The problem is that I'm not sure how to allow the Queue file to accept asynchronous calls to push new data onto the queue structure. Seeing as startServer is a per-session environment, what must I consider as I implement a shared queue.

Links that I am using for reference:

Asynchronous calls https://www.rforge.net/doc/packages/background/async.html

Scoping in R shiny http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/scoping.html

Parallel package https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/parallel/doc/parallel.pdf

Thanks in advance, and please let me know if I missed anything.

messages.subject: Is it possible to access websockets from within Shiny?
messages.subject_clean: Is it possible to access websockets from within Shiny?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I currently have an OAuth2 callback that places parameters into the URL of a shiny app, which are read for authentication. The auth flow is actually closing down the initial Shiny instance, going to the OAuth permission screen, then relaunching a new Shiny session with the auth parameters enabled in the same browser window.  This has been working fine, but it's a bit annoying if users refresh the page as the URL is then out of date and it's not obvious why authentication doesn't work. It also means it can't be used in iframes and stuff like flexdashboard, that don't let you access the URL (?)

httr that it's built upon uses websockets to authenticate when working locally, so I wondered if this was also possible when in a Shiny environment.  I'm not clear on how websockets work, and from others I heard it may depend on certain ports being open on the server, but I wanted to ask if it's possible to instead redirect an OAuth to a websockets instead, in a manner that the Shiny app can pick up its URL parameters. That way I can keep a clean URL for users browsers, I hope. :)

Yours sincerely,
Mark

messages.subject_clean: Unbinding two DataTables in tabset panels behaves oddly
messages.body_plain:
Maybe it's that the tables, like all outputs, aren't actually rendered if they're not showing. You can override this behavior in your Shiny Server function with:

outputOptions(output, "x1", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
outputOptions(output, "x2", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)

Hey Joe,

I realize now that this does not actually solve the problem. When you change the outputOptions both tables render, but they do not render correctly when the sidebar changes. Consider this slightly modified example:

library(shiny)
library(DT)
shinyApp(
  ui = fluidPage(
    sidebarPanel(
      # choose dataset
      selectInput("select","Choose dataset",c("mtcars","iris"))),
    # display table
    mainPanel(
      tabsetPanel(tabPanel("one",DT::dataTableOutput('x1')),
                  tabPanel("two",DT::dataTableOutput('x2'))),
      tags$script(HTML("Shiny.addCustomMessageHandler('unbind-DT', function(id) {
                       Shiny.unbindAll($('#'+id).find('table').DataTable().table().node());
                       })")))),

  server = function(session, input, output) {
    # function for dynamic inputs in DT
    shinyInput <- function(FUN,id,num,...) {
      inputs <- character(num)
      for (i in seq_len(num)) {
        inputs[i] <- as.character(FUN(paste0(id,i),label=NULL,...))
      }
      inputs
    }
    # function to read DT inputs
    shinyValue <- function(id,num) {
      unlist(lapply(seq_len(num),function(i) {
        value <- input[[paste0(id,i)]]
        if (is.null(value)) NA else value
      }))
    }
    # reactive dataset
    data <- reactive({
      req(input$select)
      session$sendCustomMessage('unbind-DT', 'x1')
      get(input$select)[1:5,1:3]
    })
    data2 <- reactive({
      req(input$select)
      session$sendCustomMessage('unbind-DT', 'x2')
      get(input$select)[5:10,1:3]
    })
    # render datatable with inputs
    output$x1 <- DT::renderDataTable({
      data.frame(data(),ENTER = shinyInput(numericInput,"numin",nrow(data()),value=NULL))
    },server=FALSE,escape=FALSE,selection='none',
    options=list(language = list(search = 'Filter:'),preDrawCallback=JS(
      'function() {
      Shiny.unbindAll(this.api().table().node());}'),
      drawCallback= JS(
        'function(settings) {
        Shiny.bindAll(this.api().table().node());}')))

    output$x2 <- DT::renderDataTable({
      data.frame(data2(),ENTER = shinyInput(numericInput,"numin2",nrow(data2()),value=NULL))
    },server=FALSE,escape=FALSE,selection='none',
    options=list(language = list(search = 'Filter:'),preDrawCallback=JS(
      'function() {
      Shiny.unbindAll(this.api().table().node());}'),
      drawCallback= JS(
        'function(settings) {
        Shiny.bindAll(this.api().table().node());}')))

    outputOptions(output, "x1", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
    outputOptions(output, "x2", suspendWhenHidden = FALSE)
  }

 )

Both tables render now, but when I change the selectizeInput on the sidebar, only the table in the open tab updates.

So to reproduce:

1. Run app and see that the table in each tab has a subset of mtcars

2. Change the input on the sidebar to Iris

3. You'll notice the current table now has Iris data, but if you change the tabs the table in the other tab will still have mtcars even though Iris is selected

I'm not sure what the best way to ensure that an element in an unopened tab reacts correctly, so I would appreciate some guidance.

Kind Regards,
Carl
